articles.title: Fastest century in cricket: Why Percy Fender’s 35-minute first-class hundred from 1920 remains unbeaten after 106 years
articles.summary: Cricket News: The fastest century in first-class cricket by time spent at the crease was scored more than a century ago, yet the record remains intact. Percy Fender.
articles.body: The fastest century in first-class cricket by time spent at the crease was scored more than a century ago, yet the record remains intact. Percy Fender smashed his hundred in just 35 minutes for Surrey against Northamptonshire at Northampton on August 26, 1920 — and despite several later centuries being completed in less time, none have been accepted as a genuine challenge to his mark.Fender’s record has survived because cricket’s record books make an important distinction between a breathtaking batting assault and a century produced in deliberately staged circumstances.Steve O’Shaughnessy equalled Fender’s 35-minute mark for Lancashire against Leicestershire in 1983, while centuries have since been timed at even quicker rates. But those performances came in matches where the bowling and circumstances were manipulated to force a result or achieve specific objectives.As a result, Fender’s 35-minute hundred remains widely regarded as the fastest authentic first-class century in terms of time taken.Fender turns Northamptonshire attack into recordFour days after his 28th birthday, Fender walked out for Surrey in a County Championship match that would become one of the most remarkable batting spectacles of his career.Northamptonshire made 306 in their first innings, with Fanny Walden scoring 128. Fender contributed with the ball, taking three wickets.Surrey initially found themselves in trouble at 160 for four after Andy Sandham fell for 92. But Andy Ducat and Alan Peach transformed the innings, adding 288 in just 135 minutes. Ducat eventually fell for 149, leaving Fender to take centre stage.What followed was extraordinary.Fender attacked almost from the moment he arrived, unleashing booming drives, fierce cuts, pulls and trademark slashes. He raced to his fifty in just 19 minutes, with Northamptonshire struggling to find a way of slowing him down.Gilbert Jessop had previously held the record for the fastest first-class century, reaching three figures in 40 minutes against Yorkshire at Harrogate in 1897.Fender went five minutes faster. He eventually reached his century in 35 minutes.Fender went on to score 113 in 42 minutesFender did not slow down after reaching the landmark.He finished unbeaten on 113 from 42 minutes, hitting 16 fours and five sixes. Remarkably, 94 of his 113 runs came in boundaries, meaning more than 83 per cent of his score came from fours and sixes.Surrey declared once Peach reached his double-century. Peach finished unbeaten on 203, while the sixth-wicket pair had added 171 runs in only 42 minutes.The speed of Fender’s innings was extraordinary even by modern T20 standards.Yet the record is not simply about how many balls Fender faced. It is specifically a record for the time elapsed while the batter was at the crease, an older method of measuring batting speed that differs from modern balls-faced records.That distinction is crucial when discussing the “fastest century” in cricket.The 1983 century that matched Fender — but did not countFor 63 years, Fender stood alone. Then came Steve O’Shaughnessy.The Lancashire all-rounder scored a century in 35 minutes against Leicestershire in 1983, apparently matching Fender’s record. But the circumstances surrounding the innings made it impossible to treat it as an equivalent achievement.The match had been disrupted by bad weather, with play beginning late. By the final day, both teams had specific incentives to accelerate proceedings.After Leicestershire declared, O’Shaughnessy and Graeme Fowler walked out for Lancashire against an attack that included David Gower and James Whitaker.What followed was described as farcical.Gower and Whitaker bowled a succession of full tosses and long hops, while the short boundary made attacking cricket even easier. Fowler smashed 100, including 10 sixes, while O’Shaughnessy also raced to three figures.He reached his century in 35 minutes — but the innings was effectively produced under manufactured conditions designed to accelerate scoring.Why faster centuries are not recognisedO’Shaughnessy was not the only batter to score faster than Fender.Glen Chapple hit a century in 21 minutes for Lancashire against Glamorgan in 1993. Mark Pettini scored one in 24 minutes for Essex against Leicestershire in 2006, while Michael Goodwin and Tom Moody also produced centuries in 25 and 26 minutes respectively.But these innings belong to the category of centuries that do not count for the genuine time-based record.Manufactured declarations and deliberately friendly bowling were once a feature of County Championship cricket, particularly when matches were played over three days. Captains sometimes had to find extraordinary ways of creating enough time for a result after weather interruptions or slow play.Part-time bowlers delivering full tosses and long hops could turn an innings into a boundary-hitting exercise. Although the runs officially counted in the match scorecard, records created under such conditions have generally been regarded as staged and unsuitable for comparison.That leaves Fender’s 1920 performance as the benchmark.Fastest centuries depend on how ‘fastest’ is measuredThere is another important distinction.If “fastest century” is measured by balls faced, rather than time spent at the crease, the first-class record belongs to David Hookes, who scored 102 from just 34 balls for South Australia against Victoria in 1982.In Test cricket, Brendon McCullum holds the record, scoring his century from 54 balls against Australia in Christchurch in 2016.But by elapsed time in genuine first-class conditions, Fender remains the man to beat.More than 100 years after he unleashed his extraordinary attack on Northamptonshire, no legitimate first-class innings has bettered his 35-minute mark.And that is why, despite several faster-looking centuries appearing in the record books, Percy Fender’s 35-minute hundred from 1920 remains the gold standard for the fastest authentic first-class century by time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cricket side under fire after signing player acquitted of rape, indecent assault charges
articles.summary: Cricket News: Hampshire have faced a strong reaction from their own supporters after including controversial New Zealand cricketer Scott Kuggeleijn in their squad f.
articles.body: Hampshire have faced a strong reaction from their own supporters after including controversial New Zealand cricketer Scott Kuggeleijn in their squad for the County Championship match against Warwickshire, despite not publicly announcing his signing.The 34-year-old was listed among Hampshire’s 15 players on X, with the county yet to officially confirm his arrival as an overseas player.Fans quickly criticised the move, with one calling it “a disgrace” and another describing it as “shameful” and “a new low for the club”.Kuggeleijn’s controversial pastKuggeleijn was charged in 2015 with sexual violation by rape and indecent assault involving two separate complainants. He was acquitted after a second trial, following a hung jury in the first trial.Despite the acquittal, his selection for New Zealand and domestic teams has repeatedly led to protests. In 2019, spectators at Eden Park held up posters objecting to his inclusion.Kuggeleijn has spent the past 12 years playing for Northern Districts in New Zealand and will now join Hampshire for the final four matches of their County Championship campaign.Hampshire fighting to avoid relegationHampshire are currently bottom of Division One and are 16 points behind Leicestershire, whom they still have to face.With the team battling to stay in the top division, Kuggeleijn’s arrival has added controversy away from the field.His inclusion has already sparked criticism from supporters, particularly because the club did not announce his signing before naming him in the squad.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2014, India made mid-tour coaching shake-up during England tour, brought in Ravi Shastri and new assistant coaches; how did MS Dhoni's team perform then? Revisiting as Pakistan tear up Test squad, drop seven players and two coaches after going 0-2 down in England
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan pushed the panic button and made major changes to their Test setup after losing the first two Tests against England, dropping seven players a.
articles.body: Pakistan pushed the panic button and made major changes to their Test setup after losing the first two Tests against England, dropping seven players and replacing two members of the coaching staff ahead of the third and final Test in Birmingham.After a 194-run defeat at Lord's, which gave England an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) decided to overhaul both the squad and the support staff.Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul have been called back to Pakistan. They will be replaced by white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke for the final Test starting on September 9.The PCB has also sent home seven players. Wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan, opener Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, spinner Ali Usman and fast bowler Khurram Shahzad, many of whom featured in the Lord's Test, have been dropped from the squad. All-rounder Aamir Jamal and batter Awais Zafar have also returned home without playing a match on the tour.Sarfaraz's three-month spell as head coach ended after Pakistan lost five of their six away Tests under him — two against Bangladesh, one against the West Indies and two against England.Babar Azam's return as Test captain has also failed to improve Pakistan's results. He replaced Shan Masood as captain in May and drew the West Indies series 1-1 before Pakistan lost the first two Tests in England.Pakistan have now lost 10 of their last 11 away Test matches.When India changed coaches during the England tour in 2014India made similar changes during their tour of England in 2014 after a poor Test series.India won the second Test at Lord’s to go 1-0 up in the five-match series before losing the next three heavily, including a humiliating innings and 244-run defeat within three days at The Oval in the final outing.After the series defeat, the BCCI reshuffled the support staff for the ODI series against England.Former India captain Ravi Shastri was appointed Director of Cricket, while Duncan Fletcher continued as head coach.The BCCI also gave bowling coach Joe Dawes and fielding coach Trevor Penney a "break" for the ODI series. Sanjay Bangar and former India fast bowler Bharat Arun joined as assistant coaches, while R. Sridhar became the fielding coach.The BCCI had said: "In their continuing efforts to re-energise the support to the team, the BCCI has given a break to the bowling coach Mr Joe Dawes and the fielding coach, Mr Trevor Penny for the one day series and appointed Mr Sanjay Bangar, former Indian all rounder and former India fast bowler Mr Bharat Arun as the Asst. coaches of the team. Mr R.Sridhar will join the support team as the fielding coach for the one day series."India went on to win the five-match ODI series 3-1. After first ODI was washed out in Bristol, India went on to win the next three games in Cardiff, Nottingham, and Bermingham, respectively, before losing the last ODI in Leeds.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WTC dreams run into scheduling roadblock: Irani Cup, Asian Games and ODIs leave little room to prepare before New Zealand and Australia series
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: With India down to fifth in the World Test Championship (WTC) standings, the team management and national selectors have been left coping w.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With India down to fifth in the World Test Championship (WTC) standings, the team management and national selectors have been left coping with a congested schedule as they prepare for the two remaining Test assignments of the cycle - against New Zealand in November and the five-Test Border-Gavaskar Trophy (BGT) against Australia at home beginning on January 21, 2027.TOI understands that Test captain Shubman Gill has suggested that India's batters be given quality match practice on pitches offering a reasonable amount of turn against Australia 'A' in Puducherry this month. However, the BCCI has drawn up a schedule in which the second of the two four-day matches overlaps with the Irani Cup.At the same time, two separate India squads will be involved in the Asian Games and the three-match ODI series against the West Indies from late September to early October. The overlap leaves the selectors with little room to provide the Test players with adequate red-ball preparation against Australia 'A'."Indian batters have not been at their best against spin at home over the last two years. Gill suggested that if a few batters could be given game time against Australia 'A', with the pitches taking some turn during the course of the matches, it would help them prepare for the BGT. Obviously, the touring Australian 'A' team won't be given absolute rank turners with an eye on the BGT, but it wouldn't hurt if the pitches took some turn later in the match," a BCCI source said."The problem with the schedule is that there will be very few Test players available for the 'A' match. Otherwise, the Rest of India team for the Irani Cup will not be as strong as the selectors would like it to be, and that could affect the standard of the match," the source added.The two four-day red-ball matches against Australia 'A' are scheduled for Sept 22-25 and Sept 29-Oct 2. The Irani Cup will be played in Srinagar from Oct 1-5.With several leading T20I players travelling for the Asian Games, the selectors may have to draw on their reserve pool for the three-match ODI series against the West Indies, beginning on Sept 27. It has also been learnt that VVS Laxman, who will serve as head coach at the Asian Games, has requested four additional net bowlers for the event amid concerns over accommodation arrangements for the contingent.Nearly 60 players on NZ visa list as Test preparation is squeezed:The scheduling problems have also spilled over into preparations for the New Zealand Tests. TOI has learnt that the board has drawn up a list of nearly 60 players for visa applications.India's tour begins with five T20Is on Oct 22. India 'A' will play three four-day, red-ball matches from Oct 24, overlapping with the five-match ODI series. The first Test is scheduled to begin just four days after the last ODI. "The team management was asked to spell out its preparatory plans for the NZ series. Since so many matches have been packed into a tight schedule, a list of around 60 players was shared to get the visas ready. The selectors and the team management are in a difficult position as they work out a plan to prepare the players for the Test series," BCCI sources said.Sources said the team management and selectors are keen to release key Test players from the ODI squad after the third ODI, giving them sufficient time to prepare for the Tests. Gill and head coach Gautam Gambhir have been vocal about wanting at least 10 to 14 days of preparation before a marquee Test series."With the India 'A' red-ball series overlapping with the ODI series, some of the key Test players may have to be pressed into playing an India 'A' match before the ODIs, which would not be ideal preparation for the ODIs, especially with the World Cup barely a year away. The team management would have liked to field its full ODI side to prepare for the bouncy and seaming conditions in South Africa next year. But slipping up in this Test series could end India's WTC campaign," said a source.Coordination gap within BCCI?The BCCI's operations team usually charts the schedule in coordination with the CoE, the Indian team management and the selectors. Such coordination became standard when Rahul Dravid was in charge of India's developmental sides and the erstwhile National Cricket Academy, now the CoE.However, sources said the Indian team management was not involved in drawing up the season's fixtures. The BCCI had accommodated Gill's request for adequate preparation time while planning the recently concluded tour of Sri Lanka.But the current schedule has made it difficult for Gill and the team management to prepare for the New Zealand tour and the BGT.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Duleep Trophy: East Zone in final with dominant victory over Central
articles.summary: Cricket News: BENGALURU: On a day when 13 wickets fell, East Zone had the final say in the Duleep Trophy semifinal at the BCCI CoE here. The Ishan Kishan-led side d.
articles.body: BENGALURU: On a day when 13 wickets fell, East Zone had the final say in the Duleep Trophy semifinal at the BCCI CoE here. The Ishan Kishan-led side dominated proceedings in the second innings to claim a four-wicket victory over Central Zone to reach the final.With East set a target of 159 runs, the 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (40) and Ishan Kishan (39 n.o.) helped their team to reach the target with a day to spare on Tuesday. It was for the second straight match that East, who beat Northeast in the quarterfinal, wrapped up the match inside three days.All eyes were again on Vaibhav during the chase. Interestingly, there was a slight change in Vaibhav's approach. The Bihar boy, who hit only one six in his first 37 balls, cut loose in the 14th over to smash Yash Thakur for three fours and a six before his dismissal. Another attempted six off Thakur ended his innings with Central skipper Rajat Patidar taking a fine running catch.Though slow left-arm Harsh Dubey claimed four wickets -- Abhimanyu Easwaran, Virat Singh, Kumar Kushagra, Anukul Roy -- quickly, Ishan saw East home.Earlier, Central, who started the day on 45/3, lost wickets at regular intervals. Mukesh Kumar finished with a four-wicket haul while Mohammed Shami claimed three as Central lost their last seven wickets in the morning session.North zone fightbackIn the other semifinal, North Zone batters showed positive intent at the adjacent ground after South stretched their lead to 117. North, who were sitting pretty at 175/2, were reduced to 256/7 at stumps as they took their lead to 139 runs at the end of the penultimate day's play.The Delhi duo of Sanat Sangwan (76) and Ayush Doseja (52) kept the scoreboard ticking. However, pacer Vidwath Kaverappa, who did not take the field in the third session due to a leg injury, dismissed Doseja. New man Ayush Badoni then kept the momentum going with a brisk 37-ball 31, but North lost the plot after tea.In a span of 10 overs, South took five wickets before Nishant Sindhu (20 batting) and Anshul Kamboj (29 batting) stitched an unbeaten 47-run eighth-wicket stand to keep their side afloat. Earlier, South added 27 runs to their overnight total of 285/9 before being all out. Tilak Verma remained unbeaten on 116.Brief scores: North Zone 195 & 256/7 in 66 overs (Sanat Sangwan 76, Ayush Doseja 52, Anshul Kamboj 29 batting; MD Nidheesh 2-47, Kavuri Saiteja 2-34, Shreyas Gopal 2-77) vs. South 312 (o/n: 285/9) in 100.3 overs (Tilak Varma 116 n.o; Arshdeep Singh 2-59, Anshul 2-58, Gurnoor Brar 4-88).Central 266 & 158 (o/n: 45/3) in 50.2 overs (Aman Mokhade 41; Mukesh Kumar 4-44, Mohammed Shami 3-56) lost to East 266 & 162/6 in 39.3 overs (Vaibhav Sooryavanshi 40, Ishan Kishan 39; Harsh Dubey 4-53).Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'The more you bowl, the stronger you become': Gurnoor Brar
articles.summary: Cricket News: Bengaluru: In a crowded Indian pace pool, opportunities have to be seized. Punjab's Gurnoor Brar appears to have taken that lesson to heart. The lanky.
articles.body: Bengaluru: In a crowded Indian pace pool, opportunities have to be seized. Punjab's Gurnoor Brar appears to have taken that lesson to heart. The lanky pacer made an immediate impression on his India ODI debut against Afghanistan in June, claiming three wickets. A month later, representing India 'A', he followed it up with a 10-wicket match haul against Sri Lanka 'A' in Galle.Brar's schedule has been relentless. He flew in from Sri Lanka on Friday and turned up for the Duleep Trophy semifinal against South Zone at the BCCI Centre of Excellence on Sunday. Despite bowling 23 overs on a slow-paced surface, he maintained his intensity and finished with a four-wicket match haul in the first innings.For now, though, workload is not something that worries the 25-year-old. He believes the demands of fast bowling are best embraced rather than feared. "I have always believed in training my body to high loads. No matter how much I bowl, it should not matter. I enjoy bowling more. Breaks are needed, obviously, but it is all planning. And the more we push our bodies, the stronger they get. I have an old fast bowler's mindset: the more you bowl, the stronger you become."Brar's rise has been built on sustained performances. He took 30 wickets from nine matches in the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, earned his maiden Test call-up for the one-off Afghanistan Test and was subsequently picked for the Sri Lanka tour. The speedster is yet to make his Test debut but the last three months have offered an invaluable lesson alongside Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna and other seniors."I was performing well in the Ranji Trophy; I also did well for India 'A' and I was picked on that basis. But I've learned how to stay consistent with my lengths and bowl on different wickets. I've been growing well under Morne sir (bowling coach Morkel), Gambhir sir (head coach), 'Boom' (Jasprit Bumrah), Siraj and Prasidh. Seeing them prepare, I have developed," said Brar, who has taken 11 wickets in six ODIs.The biggest lesson from the senior pros, he said, was not to abandon what brought him this far. "The learnings from Bumrah and other seniors were to stick to my strengths and not change. But the important thing is to understand bowling in different conditions. Things come along with the experience of playing more matches," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pakistan cricket in turmoil: PCB selector demands inquiry into Imam-ul-Haq injury after opener didn't bat at Lord's
articles.summary: Cricket News: A senior member of Pakistan's selection committee has questioned the seriousness of Imam-ul-Haq's calf injury and called for an inquiry after the open.
articles.body: A senior member of Pakistan's selection committee has questioned the seriousness of Imam-ul-Haq's calf injury and called for an inquiry after the opener did not bat in either innings during Pakistan's 194-run defeat to England in the second Test at Lord's.Aaqib Javed, who is part of Pakistan's four-member selection panel, said the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) will investigate how Imam was managed after suffering the injury during the match."An inquiry will be conducted into this matter," Aaqib Javed told Pakistan's private news channel Geo TV during an interview aired on Tuesday night, as quoted by news agency AP.Javed questioned how a player could miss both innings because of a muscle injury."How is it possible that you failed to come out to bat in both innings after pulling up a muscle?" Javed said.He added that players have batted through injuries in the past and described Imam's case as a matter of concern."Injuries do occur and we have seen instances in the past where players -- even with casts -- have gone out and made an effort. This situation is different. It is a matter of great concern, and action will be taken regarding it."Imam injured his calf while fielding on the opening day of the Lord's Test and took no further part in the match.After former chief selector Mohammad Wasim questioned Imam's absence, the opener appeared on the outfield before play on the fourth day. He was seen shadow batting with his left calf heavily strapped but was visibly limping.Imam was one of seven players recalled from England after Pakistan lost the first two Tests at Headingley and Lord's. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were also sent back by the PCB.Pakistan have appointed white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke to take charge of the team for the third Test, which starts in Birmingham on September 9.The selectors have picked five uncapped players for the final Test, along with openers Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, who have played a combined 10 Tests.Javed also addressed reports of differences between the selectors and the team management over the playing XI for the Lord's Test.According to Javed, he wanted the team to include fast-bowling all-rounder Ubaid Shah, wicketkeeper-batter Ghazi Ghori and another pace option instead of Mohammad Rizwan. Instead, only Salman Ali Agha was dropped after leading Pakistan in the first Test in Babar Azam's absence."We can't just keep waiting,” Javed said. “I had actually spoken to both the captain and the coach after the first Test, suggesting they include Ubaid, who bowls at 140 kph. Agha was rightly rested, Ghazi Ghori was available on the tour and should have played instead of Rizwan."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 140 kmph, Rs 21.5 lakh and a dream: Shubham Gautam's rise from Narora
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Shubham Gautam hails from Narora, a town located on the banks of the Ganga River in the Bulandshahr district of Uttar Pradesh. Narora is fa.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shubham Gautam hails from Narora, a town located on the banks of the Ganga River in the Bulandshahr district of Uttar Pradesh. Narora is famous for its nuclear power plant, operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).In the NPCIL campus, Ankit Kumar Rajput runs a cricket academy, where he first spotted Shubham Gautam, a fast bowler who earlier this year won the speed hunt organised by the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA) and went on to become one of the most expensive players in the UPT20 League when Noida Kings roped him in for Rs 21.50 lakh."He has always had this good athletic body. He came to our academy when he was 14, and from that age, you could sense that the boy was different from the others," Rajput, Gautam's coach, tells TimesofIndia.com.Rajput says it is not easy for cricketers to break out from Narora, and Shubham has been an anomaly."It is one of the most backward areas of Uttar Pradesh. Cricket-wise also, you don't see anyone pursuing the sport once they pass their Class XII boards. Shubham has been different. He has been picked for the UP U-19 camps a couple of times. It was just that he never made the cut, but he was very serious about his cricket. He kept chasing his dream, and now he is living it. For someone from our area to be able to play cricket at the professional level, one needs to be special, and he is," says a proud coach.Gautam, 21, has not yet set the Uttar Pradesh T20 League on fire. The playing XI combination hasn't helped, as he has featured in only four games so far, but he has consistently hit the 140 kmph mark in the 12 overs he has bowled in the tournament.He has always had this good athletic body. He came to our academy when he was 14, and from that age, you could sense that the boy was different from the others.But for Gautam, it is not a big deal because he has always had to wait for his chances."I played district cricket but never played for Uttar Pradesh at the age-group level. I used to play tennis-ball cricket, and I started playing with a leather ball in 2017. Every year, I used to reach the final round in the trials, but this time I put in more effort. That helped me get this opportunity," he narrates his journey to this website."My father is a farmer, and farming these days is not easy. But he always supported my dream, and I guess being the youngest among the four siblings also helped me," he says.The windfall at the UPT20 auction has changed the fortunes of Gautam."I never imagined that I would go for such a big amount at the auction. I was tired and sleeping when the auction was happening, and then I found out about it. To be honest, I was a bit emotional," says Gautam, who idolises Jofra Archer.For Gautam, bowling quick and making batters dance to his tunes with his length is something that he cherishes the most."Jofra Archer is the fast bowler who inspires me the most," he says."My strength is my pace, but I have also learnt to hit the right lengths. In UPT20, I have seen that if you miss your length, batters can hit the ball from one place and send it out of the ground from another," he adds.Recently, it has been a lot of firsts for Gautam."Before this, I had only played day-night matches in private tournaments. I had never played in a league like this. My focus is on doing well in these matches. If I perform well here, it will help me in the future. My next aim is to play for Uttar Pradesh," he says.Back in Narora, Ankit Kumar Rajput, who has seen Gautam's rise from close quarters, says his ward playing in the UP League has increased the number of players at his academy."Narora has a cricketing hero now," laughs Rajput.Ankit shares an interesting story about Gautam, which tells a lot about the individual the youngster is."He never had a phone. The first one he got was two years ago, and that too in a tournament held in Aligarh, where he was the best bowler. He has always been a hustler, and in the future, you will hear a lot about him," he says.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Blow to Stephen Fleming: CSK legend rejects England Test batting coach job ahead of 2027 Ashes
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former Australia batter Michael Hussey has turned down the opportunity to become England’s Test batting coach and is instead set to join Cricket Austr.
articles.body: Former Australia batter Michael Hussey has turned down the opportunity to become England’s Test batting coach and is instead set to join Cricket Australia in a part-time consultancy role. The decision comes as a boost for Australia ahead of next year’s Ashes and leaves England Test head coach Stephen Fleming searching for another batting coach.According to a report in The Guardian, Hussey preferred the Australia role because its flexible nature will allow him to continue his existing commitments in franchise cricket, The Hundred and commentary. The 51-year-old had spoken to Fleming last month about joining England’s coaching staff but has decided to remain in Australia.The report said the flexibility offered by Cricket Australia was a key factor in Hussey’s decision, compared with the more demanding role proposed by England and Fleming.Hussey was Welsh Fire’s head coach in The Hundred this year and has also worked as a batting coach for Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League.Fleming and Hussey worked together for 18 years at CSK, first as player and coach, before their association ended this year. Fleming was unable to convince his former colleague to join him with England.Hussey had previously worked with England as a part-time consultant during their successful T20 World Cup campaign in 2022. However, taking up a full-time role as Test batting coach would have involved a heavier workload, with England scheduled to tour South Africa, Bangladesh and Australia this winter before hosting the Ashes next summer.Australia’s Test schedule is also demanding, but Hussey will be able to work around his other commitments under the part-time arrangement.Fleming can continue looking for a batting coach, although the England and Wales Cricket Board could decide to retain Marcus Trescothick. The poor run continued in England, where India lost the five-match T20I series 4-0. The 125-run defeat in Nottingham was the team's biggest loss of the series. Under Shubman Gill's captaincy, India also lost the ODI series in England 2-1.A source said the review will not be limited to those tours.“Not just the tours of the UK, the tours of Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka will be reviewed as well,” a source said.The meeting is also expected to focus on player injury management ahead of India's upcoming Test assignments.India will travel to New Zealand in November for a two-Test series, and the BCCI wants to review the growing number of injury concerns in the squad.After the third ODI against England at Lord's, Gill had expressed frustration over frequent injuries affecting the team during overseas tours.Jasprit Bumrah missed the Sri Lanka tour after aggravating his left knee injury.Even for India's T20I series against Afghanistan, announced on Tuesday, the availability of four players is still uncertain. articles.title: Tilak Varma's fifty seals South Zone's seven-wicket win, books Duleep Trophy final  against East Zone
articles.summary: Cricket News: South Zone booked their place in the Duleep Trophy final with a convincing seven-wicket win over North Zone, with captain Tilak Varma finishing the jo.
articles.body: South Zone booked their place in the Duleep Trophy final with a convincing seven-wicket win over North Zone, with captain Tilak Varma finishing the job with a patient half-century at the BCCI Centre of Excellence Ground 2 in Bengaluru on Wednesday.Chasing 181 for victory, South Zone reached 182/3, with Tilak unbeaten on 51. R Smaran provided him company in an unbeaten 79-run partnership as South Zone completed the chase with plenty to spare.Nidheesh's five-for leaves North Zone with modest targetNorth Zone, resuming Day 4 on 256/7 with a lead of 139, managed to add only 41 runs before being bowled out for 297. Anshul Kamboj and Nishant Sindhu extended their partnership to 60 before Kamboj was dismissed by MD Nidheesh for 36.Gurnoor Brar and Arshdeep Singh struck a six each, but Nidheesh cleaned up both batters to complete a five-wicket haul. He finished with 5/56 as North Zone folded, leaving Sindhu stranded on 35.Tilak and Smaran finish the chase in styleSouth Zone began their chase steadily with Ricky Bhui and Narayan Jagadeesan adding 64 for the opening wicket. Bhui took the attacking route, hitting seven fours in a 53-ball 42 before falling to Brar. Shaik Rasheed was then bowled by Abid Mushtaq for one, but Jagadeesan and Tilak ensured there was no further damage before lunch, taking South Zone to 72/2.The pair continued to consolidate in the second session and took South Zone beyond 100 before Jagadeesan was stumped off Mushtaq for 43. With the target still within reach, Tilak joined forces with Smaran to put the result beyond doubt.Tilak struck two boundaries off Kamboj and another against Mushtaq, while Smaran attacked Ayush Badoni's offspin with a couple of boundaries of his own. North Zone's decision to turn to part-time options in the closing stages underlined their fading hopes.Tilak eventually sealed victory with a boundary that also brought up his half-century.First-innings hundred laid the foundationThe South Zone captain had already played the defining innings of the match in the first innings, scoring an unbeaten 116 after his side had slipped to 80/5 while chasing North Zone's 195. His 175-run partnership with Shreyas Gopal, who made 87, helped South Zone take a crucial 117-run first-innings lead.North Zone briefly fought back through fifties from Sanat Sangwan and Ayush Doseja, but their second-innings collapse on Day 3 left them with too much to do. South Zone will face East Zone in the final at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai from September 6 after East Zone defeated Central Zone by four wickets in the other semifinal.Brief Scores: North Zone 195 & 297 (Sanat Sangwan 76, Ayush Doseja 52; MD Nidheesh 5/56, Kavuri Saiteja 2/57) lost to South Zone 312 & 182/3 (Tilak Varma 51*, Narayan Jagadeesan 43, Ricky Bhui 42; Abid Mushtaq 2/55) by seven wickets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Questions over 'character', players removed without communication: How Pakistan's day of chaos unfolded after England humiliation
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan cricket was thrown into chaos after the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) made sweeping changes following the team's defeats in the first two Test.
articles.body: Pakistan cricket was thrown into chaos after the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) made sweeping changes following the team's defeats in the first two Tests against England, with several players reportedly finding out they had been dropped only through social media posts instead of being informed by the team management.The PCB recalled seven players and replaced two coaches after Pakistan lost the series 2-0 against England.Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were also sent home and replaced by white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke for the third and final Test in Birmingham, starting on September 9.Wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan, injured opener Imam-ul-Haq, captain in the first Test Salman Ali Agha, spinner Ali Usman and pacer Khurram Shahzad — most of whom played in the second Test at Lord's — were also recalled from the tour. All-rounder Aamir Jamal and batter Awais Zafar returned home without playing a match in England.Players found out through social mediaAccording to a report published by UK-based newspaper The Telegraph, the way the PCB handled the overhaul left the players shocked.The report said several players were spending their day off in London or were at the team hotel when friends and family started sending them screenshots of the PCB's announcement on social media.The players had not been informed before the board made the announcement."Team management had not told them beforehand. To say they were shocked was an understatement," The Telegraph report said.The report added that the way the decision was handled left "the most bitter of tastes" inside the squad. It also said the international future of several players was suddenly thrown into doubt, with questions being raised over their "character, fitness and decision-making."No communication from captain, coach or team managementThe report said many players privately contacted friends and family after seeing the announcement, trying to understand what had happened.Several of them reportedly expressed "shock and confusion" because no direct communication had come from the team management, the captain or the coach before the PCB statement was released.One player who featured in the series reportedly felt he was being unfairly made a scapegoat despite believing he had performed well.According to the report, he was in his room at the team hotel in London when messages started arriving. A friend forwarded him the PCB press release, and he had to read it twice because he initially thought it was fake.The report also said players viewed the decision to send them home without informing them personally as degrading.The confusion continued on Tuesday, when former Pakistan captain Misbah-ul-Haq resigned from the selection committee after he was not consulted about the seven players who were recalled.Imam and Rizwan among senior players under scrutinyThe report said Pakistan's tour of England had already been marked by tension between the players and the PCB before the squad overhaul.Imam-ul-Haq is among the players whose future is under serious doubt after he did not bat in either innings at Lord's because of a calf injury.The PCB is unhappy with how the injury situation unfolded and believes it reflected poorly on both the player and the team, The Telegraph reported.Mohammad Rizwan is another senior player who was sent home after reportedly coming under scrutiny.According to the report, the PCB is unhappy with Rizwan's influence in the dressing room and feels he has become a "disruptive presence."It also said Rizwan's shot selection during the Test series frustrated senior members of the team management and officials at the board, who expected better from a player of his experience.Sarfaraz and Umar Gul removed after poor Test runThe coaching changes came after Sarfaraz Ahmed failed to improve Pakistan's Test results during his three-month stint as head coach.Babar Azam's second stint as Test captain also failed to improve the team's fortunes after Shan Masood was removed from the role in May. Pakistan drew the series in the West Indies 1-1 under Babar but lost both Tests in England.Pakistan have now lost 10 of their last 11 away Tests.Umar Gul was also removed as bowling coach. According to the report, the PCB believed he failed to get the best out of the pace attack, and his explanation that the cold weather affected Pakistan's bowlers at Leeds did not go down well with senior officials, who felt it lacked accountability.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Hampshire decide that New Zealand all-rounder Scott Kuggeleijn will not represent the club having "listened to feedback from staff and supporters".
articles.body:
Hampshire have decided that New Zealand all-rounder Scott Kuggeleijn will not represent the club having "listened to feedback from staff and supporters".

On Tuesday the Rose and Crown named him in their squad for a County Championship match against Warwickshire without announcing his signing on their social channels.

The signing received criticism on social media and less than an hour before the start of play on Wednesday the county said that Kuggeleijn would not play any role in their final four games.

Kuggeleijn, 34, faced a rape charge in 2015 and after a re-trial due to a hung jury he was acquitted in 2017.

It is understood that the player was in attendance at Utilita Bowl for the first day of the game on Wednesday.

"Having reflected and listened to feedback from staff and supporters Hampshire Cricket can confirm that Scott Kuggeleijn will not represent the club," the county said in a statement. , external

"We value the passion of our fanbase and thank everyone who took the time to share their views.

"Our focus now turns to supporting the team through the final four County Championship fixtures of the season.

"We encourage everyone to unite behind the team as we enter a crucial stage of the campaign."

Seam bowler Kuggeleijn has spent 12 years playing for Northern Districts in his home country.

He has also played three Test matches for the Black Caps as well as two one-day internationals and 18 T20s.

Hampshire currently sit bottom of Division One in the County Championships on 86 points, 16 points below Leicestershire above them.

The Rose and Crown have only won twice with the red ball this year, losing on five occasions and drawing three.

articles.summary: Cricket News: Ben Stokes is set to make his mark in the Big Bash League with the Adelaide Strikers, and coach Tim Paine believes the England all-rounder could be pa.
articles.body: Ben Stokes is set to make his mark in the Big Bash League with the Adelaide Strikers, and coach Tim Paine believes the England all-rounder could be particularly effective if he opens the batting.Stokes’ one-year deal with the Strikers was confirmed on Tuesday, making him available for the entire BBL season. Paine believes the 35-year-old can make an impact across all three departments while also bringing his leadership experience to the side. The Strikers had Matt Short and Chris Lynn as their regular opening combination last season, but Lynn is currently off contract, meaning the pair could be split up even if he returns to the franchise.Paine backs Stokes to open in BBLPaine sees Stokes as an ideal candidate to take the new ball with the bat, particularly on Australia’s traditionally pace-friendly and bouncy pitches.“Stokes gives us a lot of flexibility. I think initially my chats around how we would use him would probably be opening the batting. I think he's made to open the batting in Big Bash. I think the pacy, bouncy wickets in Australia really suit him,” Paine said, as quoted by ESPNcricinfo.The former Australia captain also highlighted Stokes’ ability to attack all areas of the ground and change the momentum of an innings almost instantly.“I have been on the end of a couple of these devastating innings in Test cricket where you feel like you cannot defend the field. He can play 360 degrees. He has got power. He has got some real class,” he added.Although Stokes has opened in only 16 of his 148 T20 innings, the numbers suggest he is at his most productive in that role. He averages 36.53 and has a strike rate of 138.48 as an opener. One of his two T20 centuries also came while opening, when he smashed an unbeaten 107 off 60 balls for Rajasthan Royals in the 2020 IPL. His other T20 century came for Rising Pune Supergiant in 2017, when he scored 103 off 63 deliveries.However, much of Stokes’ T20 career has seen him bat at No. 3, 4 or 5. He has not played a T20 match since The Hundred in 2024, where he managed only four runs across three innings.“I think he can do a terrific job opening the batting. Playing pretty normally, as we have seen in the past, he can flick a switch, and he has got amazing power. His skill level with the bat and his play of spin, he has just a well-rounded, world-class batter. We think that is probably the best fit for him and for us,” Paine said.Stokes can make impact with ball tooPaine also believes Stokes could have an impact with the ball, suggesting his pace and ability to move the ball could make him a useful option in different phases of an innings.“He is a bit quicker than people think. He has got great skill. He can swing the ball both ways. We feel like we can use him in all phases of the game with the ball as well. He will impact in the field with his athleticism and just the way he competes,” he said.Stokes has taken 352 wickets for England across international cricket, with his best figures of 6/22 highlighting his ability to produce decisive spells.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: India will host the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy in 2027, with the six-team tournament relocated from its originally designated host Sri Lan.
articles.body: India will host the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy in 2027, with the six-team tournament relocated from its originally designated host Sri Lanka. The tournament is scheduled to take place from February 14 to 28, 2027, marking a significant addition to India’s calendar of major women’s cricket events.The competition will feature six teams and will be played in the T20I format, with a total of 16 matches. India, Australia, England, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka have qualified for the tournament based on the ICC Women’s T20I Team Rankings.Mumbai, Vadodara to host matchesThe tournament will be played across two venues, the Cricket Club of India (CCI) in Mumbai and the Vadodara International Cricket Stadium. All six teams will compete in a round-robin league stage, with the top two sides advancing to the final.Sri Lanka lost hosting rights over governance concernsSri Lanka had originally been awarded hosting rights for the tournament. However, the ICC Board subsequently approved the move to India following a host evaluation process. Sri Lanka Cricket remains under a government-appointed committee, which the ICC considers a violation of its regulations concerning government or political interference in the administration of cricket.India emerged as the successful bidder after competing proposals from Bangladesh and South Africa were considered.“The ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 marks an exciting new chapter for women’s cricket,” ICC Chairman Jay Shah said.“As the inaugural edition of the tournament, it will bring together the best teams in the world in an intense, high-quality competition, while creating even greater incentive for teams to continue rising through the rankings and competing for a place on the global stage,” he added.Jay Shah also highlighted the ICC’s plans to create a stronger rhythm for women’s international cricket through a regular calendar of major events.“With a marquee ICC women’s event now taking place every year, we have a significant opportunity to build greater momentum, provide more consistency and create a stronger rhythm for the women’s game, its players and its fans around the world,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Sri Lanka had been due to stage the six-team event but have been stripped of the hosting rights because of ongoing issues with its national board and government interference.

A statement from the ICC said Sri Lanka Cricket is continuing "to make the requisite reforms" which were outlined at the global governing body's annual conference in July.

Bangladesh and South Africa were also interested in staging the tournament but the ICC board ratified India as replacement hosts for the event, with matches to be held in Mumbai and Vadodara.

Unlike the men's Champions Trophy, which is a 50-over-a-side competition, the women's event will be a T20 tournament.

It will be played on a round-robin basis with the top two sides progressing to the final.

Australia, England, India, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka are the six teams who will take part, having been the highest-ranked sides at the qualification cut-off date of 6 July.

articles.title: England cricket team: Brydon Carse omitted from squad for third Test against Pakistan
articles.summary: England leave Brydon Carse out of their squad for the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston.
articles.body:
England have omitted Brydon Carse from their squad for the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston.

The 31-year-old Durham seamer was dropped for the second Test at Lord's after he was briefly arrested following an incident outside a Derby nightclub on 22 August.

Carse's replacement, 23-year-old Sonny Baker, has retained his place in England's 15-man party.

Surrey's Matthew Fisher has been dropped from an otherwise unchanged England squad as they seek to complete a series clean-sweep over Pakistan.

The third Test in Birmingham starts on Wednesday, 9 September at 11:00 BST.

With six white-ball matches against Sri Lanka to follow the Test series, England may consider resting seamers Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue, all of whom feature in the limited-overs set-up.

While the trio have been named in the Test squad, they may be rotated in favour of Baker, Essex pace bowler Sam Cook and Derbyshire spinner Shoaib Bashir.

Cook, 29, played his one Test against Zimbabwe last summer while 22-year-old Bashir is yet to feature in this series, with England preferring an all-pace attack.

Baker made his only Test appearance to date in a much-changed line-up against New Zealand at The Oval in June.

Carse remains available for selection for Durham and finished with match figures of 4-95 in their win over Gloucestershire last week.

However, he has not been picked in the XI for their match against Northamptonshire, which started on Wednesday.

Pakistan made the extraordinary move of dropping seven players, calling up five uncapped players and releasing their head coach prior to the Edgbaston Test.

Sarfaraz Ahmed has replaced by Pakistan white-ball coach Mike Hesson, while Muhammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman and Khurram Shahzad, all of whom have featured in the series, are among the players dropped.

England beat Pakistan by an innings and 103 runs in the first Test at Headingley and sealed series victory with a win by 194 runs at Lord's last week.

articles.title: 8 wickets in 4 Innings, Yet former India WK-batter urges team to look beyond Ravindra Jadeja
articles.summary: Cricket News: Ravindra Jadeja has been a mainstay of India’s Test team for more than a decade, but former India wicketkeeper-batter Deep Dasgupta believes the time .
articles.body: Ravindra Jadeja has been a mainstay of India’s Test team for more than a decade, but former India wicketkeeper-batter Deep Dasgupta believes the time has come for the team to start looking beyond the veteran all-rounder in the longest format.Jadeja aged 37, finished India’s recent two-Test tour of Sri Lanka with eight wickets across four innings. However, Dasgupta felt the Indian spin attack failed to consistently exert pressure on the hosts, particularly on surfaces where the visitors would have expected their spinners to play a major role.The former India player singled out the second Test in Colombo, where Sri Lanka were forced to follow on but managed to fight back strongly. Sonal Dinusha’s century helped the hosts frustrate India and build a substantial lead before the match eventually ended in a draw.'Jadeja has been a great servant, but it’s done now'While Jadeja picked up three wickets in Sri Lanka’s second innings, Dasgupta felt India needed more penetration from their experienced spinners.“Apart from Manav, our spinners didn’t look as lethal as we expected. I’m not saying there is no ability. On such pitches, Jadeja has always been very destructive and lethal. I thought he would be crucial on the fifth day. He has been a great servant, but it’s done now. He was not as accurate as he is. His action is very shoulder-dominant,” Dasgupta said on his YouTube channel.Dasgupta flags no-ball issuesThe Sri Lanka series also highlighted an issue with India’s bowling discipline, with the spinners repeatedly overstepping. Saransh Jain, making his Test debut in Colombo, bowled four no-balls, while Jadeja overstepped once. Dasgupta believes such problems need to be addressed during training rather than waiting for them to surface in matches.“If you are not careful in the nets, it will happen. Even when I was playing, a lot of them would bowl from ahead and say it would not happen in the match, but they would repeat the same thing in the match. You need to avoid this in the nets. This issue is not new with Jadeja; it has only gotten worse,” he added.India won the two-match series 1-0, with victory by 165 runs in the opening Test in Galle before the second Test in Colombo ended in a draw. articles.title: Women's Champions Trophy: ICC confirm India as venue for inaugural edition after Sri Lanka removed from hosting rights
articles.summary: Australia, England, India, ​New Zealand, South Africa and Sri ​Lanka are the six teams that will ⁠compete in the inaugural ICC Women's Champions Trophy; Sri Lanka were originally announced hosts but have been replaced by India
articles.body:
The six-team tournament, taking place from February 14-28 next year, was due to be held in Sri Lanka but will now take place in the Indian cities of Mumbai and Vadodara.

Sri Lanka have lost the right to stage the tournament because of government interference in their board, with Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) currently holding an interim administration put in place by the Sri Lanka government.

The ICC said the SLC 'continue to make the requisite reforms' outlined at the ICC's Annual Conference in July, with Bangladesh and South Africa assessed as potential options before India were confirmed as host nation.

ICC Chairman, Mr. Jay Shah, said: "The ICC Women's Champions Trophy 2027 marks an exciting new chapter for women's cricket.

"As the inaugural edition of the tournament, it will bring together the best teams in the world in an intense, high-quality competition, while creating even greater incentive for teams to continue rising through the rankings and competing for a place on the global stage.

"With a marquee ICC women's event now taking place every year, we have a significant opportunity to build greater momentum, provide more consistency and create a stronger rhythm for the women's game, its players and its fans around the world."

Australia, England, India, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka are the six teams involved, based on their positions in the ICC Women's T20I Team Rankings on the July 6 qualification cut-off date.

All six teams will compete in a round-robin league, with the top two sides advancing to the final on February 28.

The matches ​will be held at the Cricket Club ​of India in Mumbai and Vadodara's International Cricket Stadium.

articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Brydon Carse left out for third and final Test at Edgbaston as Joe Root's 15-man squad revealed
articles.summary: Brydon Carse has been left out of the third Test, live from September 9-13 on Sky Sports Cricket; Carse missed second Test after being briefly arrested following an ​incident outside a Derby nightclub; Carse has also been left out of Durham squad for County Championship game
articles.body:
England are chasing a 3-0 series sweep, live from September 9-13 on Sky Sports, having thrashed the tourists by an innings and 103 runs at Headingley before claiming a 194-run victory at Lord's.

Carse was withdrawn from the squad for the second Test, after the Cricket Regulator initiated a probe into an incident that saw the Durham player briefly arrested outside a Derby nightclub on August 22.

Derbyshire Police are looking into "allegations of assault" against the 31-year-old, with right-armer Sonny Baker retaining his place in Joe Root's squad as Carse's replacement, while Fisher misses out after being unused in the first two Tests.

Carse was also left out of Durham's squad for their County Championship match against Northamptonshire, which began on Wednesday, due to 'pre-arranged workload management", despite finishing with match figures of 4-95 in their previous win over Gloucestershire.

Speaking at Lord's last week, England captain Joe Root described himself as "hacked off" by the growing number of alcohol-related stories around the team, adding: "I've spoken to Brydon and when I first found out my first concern was him as a person.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn in saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself."

England's interim head coach Marcus Trescothick has indicated a preference to field his strongest possible side in pursuit of a 3-0 scoreline, rather than ring the changes.

That means Baker and Sam Cook may be kept on the sidelines, unless it is decided that any of the in-form pace attack of Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Atkinson need to be rested.

An inexperienced Pakistan outfit have been skittled for under 200 in all four innings so far, only batting beyond 50 overs once, with the relentless accuracy of Robinson - who finished with match figures of 8-35 in the second Test, backed up brilliantly by England's other seamers.

England squad: Joe Root (Yorkshire, captain), Jofra Archer (Sussex), Gus Atkinson (Surrey), Sonny Baker (Hampshire), Shoaib Bashir (Derbyshire), Harry Brook (Yorkshire), Sam Cook (Essex), Jordan Cox (Essex), Ben Duckett (Nottinghamshire), Emilio Gay (Durham), Dan Lawrence (Surrey), Ollie Pope (Surrey), Ollie Robinson (Sussex), Jamie Smith (Surrey), Josh Tongue (Nottinghamshire)

Pakistan make wholesale changes for Test dead rubber

Pakistan have dropped seven players and two coaches from their touring squad following their series defeat to England and ahead of the final Test at Edgbaston.

Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq - injured during the second Test defeat at Lord's - Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad have all been sent home.

Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul have also been released and will be replaced by Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke in the backroom staff.

Seven replacements have been called up to the squad, including five uncapped players at Test level, with batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal having eight and two Test appearances, respectively.

Left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas has represented Pakistan in white-ball cricket, with left-arm fast bowler Mohammad Imran Jnr, wicketkeeper-batter Saad Baig and pace-bowling all-rounders Mohammad Imran (also known as Imran Randhawa) and Razaullah the others brought in.

articles.title: Rohit Sharma’s future, ODI roadmap to 2027 World Cup and recent setbacks on agenda at BCCI meeting
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mumbai/New Delhi: The future of Rohit Sharma and the shape of India’s ODI team for the next World Cup cycle are set to dominate discussions when the B.
articles.body: Mumbai/New Delhi: The future of Rohit Sharma and the shape of India’s ODI team for the next World Cup cycle are set to dominate discussions when the BCCI’s top brass meets in Mumbai on Thursday for a wide-ranging performance review.While recent defeats in Ireland, England and Sri Lanka will be assessed, board officials are understood to be more concerned about the lack of a clearly defined ODI roadmap at a time when preparations for the 2027 World Cup should be taking shape.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia, president Mithun Manhas, head coach Gautam Gambhir, chief selector Ajit Agarkar and Centre of Excellence chief VVS Laxman will attend the meeting, with ODI and Test captain Shubman Gill and T20I skipper Shreyas Iyer also expected to be present.At the centre of the discussions lies the most sensitive issue facing Indian cricket: Rohit’s future. Though there is immense respect for the veteran opener’s stature and achievements, selectors and members of the team management are increasingly aware of the need to prepare for a post-Rohit era.According to sources, one option under consideration is to evaluate Rohit’s role on a series-by-series basis rather than committing to a long-term plan through the entire World Cup cycle.“It’s very tough on a young captain like Shubman Gill when there is no clear direction. The dressing-room environment in the ODI team hasn’t been the best, especially when it comes to dealing with stalwarts,” a BCCI source said.The uncertainty around Rohit reflects a broader concern. Of India’s three national teams, the ODI side is regarded as the least settled. Injuries and workload management have prevented selectors from identifying a stable core, leaving several key positions unresolved.The fast-bowling allrounder’s role remains a particular headache. Hardik Pandya continues on a managed workload programme after recurring fitness issues, while Nitish Kumar Reddy is yet to receive full clearance following rehabilitation.“Hardik, at the moment, has been cleared to bowl six overs in a day. Reddy is still to clear his fitness tests. The ODI team doesn’t have even half of the core ODI team ready. It has to be a joint effort between the CoE and the team management to zero in on players and formulate a roadmap to get them all on the park as soon as possible,” the source said.The review was initially planned after the Ireland and England tours but was postponed because of the subsequent Sri Lanka assignment. It will now cover India’s performances across multiple tours, including Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka.India’s 2-0 T20I series defeat in Ireland and the 4-0 drubbing in England raised alarm bells, with the 125-run loss at Nottingham viewed internally as one of the team’s poorest performances in recent years. Gill’s ODI side also lost the England series 2-1.However, officials insist the exercise will focus on solutions rather than assigning blame, with particular emphasis on recurring issues in preparation, selection and execution.Fitness management is expected to be another major talking point. Jasprit Bumrah missed the Sri Lanka tour after aggravating a knee problem, while Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Harshit Rana remain in line for fitness assessments at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru on Sept 9.With a two-Test tour of New Zealand scheduled for Nov and a packed calendar ahead, the board wants tighter coordination between the medical staff, strength-and-conditioning team and national selectors to ensure greater player availability.New role for LaxmanThe meeting could also have significant administrative consequences. Laxman is being considered for an expanded role, with discussions continuing over a possible Director of Cricket position overseeing coaching, selection and player-development pathways. Agarkar’s tenure as chief selector, which ends later this month, will also come under review, with a one-year extension among the options being discussed.Board President’s XI fixture vs visiting teams may be backMeanwhile, BCCI is also examining the possibility of reviving the traditional Board President’s XI match before home series, following a recommendation from Manhas. The fixture, which historically featured leading domestic performers and Test hopefuls against visiting teams, has often served as a stepping stone for future India players while providing valuable match preparation to touring sides.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Towhid Hridoy creates history with 350, breaks Tamim Iqbal’s long-standing first-class record
articles.summary: Cricket News: Bangladesh A captain Towhid Hridoy etched his name into the country's first-class record books after becoming the first Bangladeshi batter to score 35.
articles.body: Bangladesh A captain Towhid Hridoy etched his name into the country's first-class record books after becoming the first Bangladeshi batter to score 350 runs in an innings. The landmark knock came at the NWC Oval in Potchefstroom on Wednesday, more than six years after Hridoy helped Bangladesh win the Under-19 World Cup at the same venue in 2020.Resuming the fourth day on 204, Hridoy carried his bat through the remainder of Bangladesh A's innings and finished unbeaten on 350 off 481 deliveries, hitting 27 fours and 10 sixes.His innings helped Bangladesh A declare at 676 for eight, giving them a 164-run advantage after South Africa A had posted 512 in their first innings. South Africa A reached 18 without loss before the teams settled for a draw.Hridoy breaks Tamim's recordHridoy's marathon innings made him only the third Bangladeshi batter to reach a first-class triple century. More significantly, he went past Tamim Iqbal's unbeaten 334 and Raqibul Hasan's unbeaten 313 to claim the highest first-class score by a Bangladeshi batter.He also became the first Bangladeshi to register a first-class 300-plus score outside the country.The 350 was equally significant from a South African perspective. Hridoy now owns the highest first-class score by an overseas batter in South Africa. Only one other batter has crossed the 350-run mark in a first-class innings in the country, Stephen Cook, who scored 390.Reflecting on the innings, Hridoy said the performance had given him considerable confidence and made him believe he could produce a similar effort at international level.“To be honest, this innings gave me a lot of confidence. After picking the Man of the Match trophy I was feeling that someday I will play an innings like this in the national team,” Hridoy said after the match.Tamim congratulates Hridoy after record fallsTamim Iqbal, whose 334 had stood as Bangladesh's highest first-class score, was quick to congratulate Hridoy after his record was surpassed. Tamim said scoring 350 runs in any first-class setting was an exceptional achievement, but doing so in South Africa made the feat even more remarkable.He also welcomed the fact that his record had been broken, describing Hridoy's achievement as a sign of the progress being made by Bangladeshi cricket.South Africa A nevertheless took the four-day series 1-0. The hosts had dominated the opening match in Pretoria, winning by an innings and 413 runs, before Hridoy's record-setting performance helped Bangladesh avoid defeat in the second game.The two sides will now switch to the 50-over format, with a three-match one-day series beginning in Bloemfontein on September 6.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
